title: The King Who Longed for a Child
captions: Long ago, on the banks of the river Sarayu, stood the golden city of Ayodhya.
Its king, Dasharatha, was brave and fair. His people loved him, and the kingdom had everything it needed.
But the king carried one sorrow. He had no child, and no heir to care for Ayodhya after him.
His teacher, the sage Vasishtha, told him: "Do not lose hope. Hold a sacred fire ceremony and pray with a true heart."
The fire blazed, and from it rose a shining messenger carrying a golden bowl of blessed sweet rice.
The king shared the gift among his three queens: Kausalya, Kaikeyi and Sumitra.
In time, four princes were born. All of Ayodhya rejoiced!
lesson: King Dasharatha was sad, but he did not give up. He bowed to his guru, listened to his advice, and prayed with a true heart. Our elders teach that when we pray with shraddha, do our part and wait patiently, blessings come at the right time. And when the blessing came, the king shared it.
question: Who is a guru in your life, like a parent, a grandparent or a teacher? What good advice have they given you?
card_lesson: King Dasharatha did not give up. He listened to his guru and prayed with a true heart. When we pray with shraddha, do our part and wait patiently, blessings come at the right time.
